title: Gradual bilateral tinnitus with high-frequency SNHL

stages.title: 1. Extract the clinical story
stages.prompt: Which information is most important to establish before selecting management?

options.text: Tinnitus laterality, onset/course, hearing concerns, noise exposure, otologic symptoms and impact on daily life
Only the pitch and loudness of the tinnitus
Only whether the patient wants a hearing aid

stages.feedback: A complete tinnitus history should establish the tinnitus characteristics, associated hearing/otologic concerns and functional impact before management is selected.

stages.title: 2. Interpret the findings
stages.prompt: The case provides mild-to-moderate high-frequency sensorineural hearing loss with gradual bilateral tinnitus. Which interpretation best fits the supplied case?

options.text: The tinnitus presentation is occurring alongside bilateral high-frequency SNHL and should be considered in the overall hearing-management plan
The findings prove a specific retrocochlear lesion
The normality of one low-frequency region excludes hearing-related tinnitus

stages.feedback: The supplied case links gradual bilateral tinnitus with mild-to-moderate high-frequency SNHL. The platform should avoid claiming a specific pathology that the case does not establish.

stages.title: 3. Check for red flags
stages.prompt: Based on the supplied presentation, how should red-flag screening be handled?

options.text: Screen for clinically important red flags; the gradual bilateral presentation itself does not establish a unilateral, pulsatile or acute emergency pattern
Assume that every tinnitus presentation requires emergency referral
Skip red-flag screening because the audiogram already gives the diagnosis

stages.feedback: Red-flag screening remains part of the standardized workflow. The case description does not specify a red-flag pattern requiring an emergency conclusion.

stages.title: 4. Select management
stages.prompt: Which management direction best matches the supplied case objective?

options.text: Counselling/education with an appropriate sound-therapy option, while addressing hearing needs and patient preferences
Provide a device immediately without discussing tinnitus impact, expectations or preferences
Recommend complete silence and avoidance of all environmental sound

stages.feedback: The case objective specifies selecting sound therapy and counselling. Management should also be connected to the patient's hearing needs and preferences.

stages.title: 5. Justify the decision
stages.prompt: Choose the justification that best connects the case findings to the management plan.

options.text: The gradual bilateral tinnitus occurs with high-frequency SNHL; counselling and sound-based support can be considered within an individualized management plan, with outcomes monitored over time
The tinnitus must be caused by one confirmed disease even though the case does not provide that diagnosis
Management should be identical for every patient with tinnitus

stages.feedback: Clinical reasoning requires a defensible link between the supplied findings, the management choice and the patient's needs, without over-claiming a diagnosis.

stages.title: 6. Plan follow-up
stages.prompt: What should be monitored at follow-up?

options.text: Tinnitus impact/distress, hearing-related difficulties, adherence and patient-reported benefit, with management adjusted when needed
Only whether the tinnitus has completely disappeared
No follow-up is needed after initial counselling

stages.feedback: Follow-up should evaluate meaningful patient outcomes rather than requiring complete tinnitus elimination as the only success criterion.
